name: Levetiracetam
drug_class: Pyrrolidone anticonvulsant; synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A) ligand
route_note: Oral tablets, extended-release tablets and solution; IV infusion with the same dose as oral.

discovery.note: The S-enantiomer of the ethyl analogue of piracetam, found to protect against seizures in animal kindling models despite inactivity in classical screening tests.

tagline: Widely used broad-spectrum anticonvulsant acting on synaptic vesicle protein SV2A
summary: Levetiracetam is a broad-spectrum anticonvulsant with a unique mechanism, binding the synaptic vesicle protein SV2A. Its linear kinetics, few interactions and IV formulation have made it one of the most prescribed antiseizure medicines.
mechanism: Levetiracetam binds SV2A, a protein in the membrane of synaptic vesicles involved in vesicle exocytosis. Binding is thought to modulate neurotransmitter release, reducing hypersynchronous firing; binding affinity of related compounds correlates with their anticonvulsant potency.
It also inhibits N-type calcium channels and reverses the inhibition of GABA- and glycine-gated currents by zinc and beta-carbolines, though the relevance of these effects is uncertain.
uses: Myoclonic seizures in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (adjunct)

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Keppra as adjunctive therapy for partial-onset seizures.

history.title: SV2A identified
history.detail: Lynch et al. (PNAS) identify synaptic vesicle protein 2A as the binding site.

history.title: IV formulation
history.detail: Keppra injection is approved in the US.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic levetiracetam becomes available in the US.

history.title: 3D-printed tablet
history.detail: Spritam becomes the first FDA-approved drug made by 3D printing.

history.title: Brivaracetam
history.detail: UCB's higher-affinity SV2A ligand brivaracetam (Briviact) is approved.

history.title: ESETT
history.detail: A trial (Kapur et al., NEJM) finds levetiracetam, fosphenytoin and valproate similarly effective for benzodiazepine-refractory status epilepticus.

pk.excretion: renal, about 66% unchanged; dose reduced in renal impairment

serious: Psychiatric reactions including aggression, psychosis and suicidal ideation

facts: Spritam (levetiracetam) was the first drug manufactured by 3D printing to be approved by the FDA, in 2015.
Levetiracetam was unusual in having been missed by the standard maximal electroshock and pentylenetetrazol screens.
